prerequisites.title: A Help Scout account with an invited user
prerequisites.detail: API credentials must be tied to an active, invited user in the Help Scout account, or calls return 401.

prerequisites.title: HTTPS redirect URL
prerequisites.detail: The API is HTTPS-only and the Authorization Code flow needs a redirection URL. Copy it from the Composio dashboard.

steps.title: Copy redirect URL from Composio
steps.detail: Get the callback URL from the Composio dashboard for the Help Scout auth config and check it is HTTPS.
steps.done_when: You have the redirect URL ready to paste.

steps.title: Create the OAuth2 app in Help Scout
steps.detail: Go to Your Profile > My apps, click Create My App, and enter the redirection URL.
steps.done_when: You have an application ID and secret.

steps.title: Create the Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the help_scout auth config through Composio's API with your own app ID and secret.
steps.done_when: The auth config exists in Composio.

steps.title: Test a connection with a real user
steps.detail: Connect a Help Scout account and approve the Authorization screen, whether or not already logged in.
steps.done_when: A connected account is created and an API call succeeds.

traps.title: Users must be active and invited
traps.detail: A user who is not an active, invited user in the account gets a 401 error.

traps.title: Managed app is not available
traps.detail: Do not plan on Composio's shared app for Help Scout; it is not offered, so launch needs your own app.

traps.title: Redirect URL is needed even for Client Credentials
traps.detail: Creating an app asks for a redirection URL; a placeholder works only if you use Client Credentials alone.

blockers.what_it_means: The credentials are not tied to an active, invited Help Scout user.
blockers.what_to_do: Invite the user to the Help Scout account and make sure they are active.

evidence.answer: For Google APIs, an app requesting sensitive or restricted user-data scopes may need verification before it is made publicly available, unless an exception applies.

evidence.quote: Sensitive scopes require review by Google before a Google Account can grant access and might be restricted by Google Workspace organization administrators.
evidence.answer: Sensitive scopes require Google's review before a Google Account can grant access to them.

evidence.quote: If your app is going to be used in any of the scenarios described in the following sections, you don't need to submit it for review.
evidence.answer: Apps used only in the listed scenarios do not need to be submitted for review.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: One use case is if you are the only user of your app or if your app is used by only a few users, all of whom are known personally to you.
evidence.answer: Personal use: no review is needed if the app is used only by its developer or by a few users who are all personally known to the developer.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: We recommend that you only submit your app for verification if you want to make your app available to any user with a Google Account.
evidence.answer: Apps in development or testing phases do not need verification; verification is recommended only when making the app available to any user with a Google Account.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: If your app uses a service account to access only its own data, and it doesn't access any user data (linked to a Google Account), then you don't need to submit for verification.
evidence.answer: Apps that use a service account to access only their own data, with no access to user data linked to a Google Account, do not need verification.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: In this case, your app might need approval from an organization administrator.
evidence.answer: Internal use within one Google Workspace or Cloud Identity organization may need approval from an organization administrator instead of verification.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: This is because a domain-wide installation lets a domain administrator grant third-party and internal applications access to your users' data.
evidence.answer: Domain-wide installation: if the app uses restricted or sensitive scopes, app verification is still required.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Submitting your app for verification involves confirming policy compliance, keeping contact information current, using the Cloud Console Verification Center, declaring all scopes, and providing detailed justification and a video demonstration for sensitive scopes.
evidence.answer: Verification submission involves confirming policy compliance and providing a detailed justification and a video demonstration for sensitive scopes.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Prepare a detailed justification for each requested sensitive scope, as well
evidence.answer: The developer must provide a detailed justification for each sensitive scope, including why a narrower scope is not sufficient.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Show the OAuth grant process that users will experience, in English.
evidence.answer: The demonstration video must show the OAuth grant process in English, including the consent flow and any sign-in flow.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Show that the OAuth consent screen correctly displays the App Name.
evidence.answer: The demonstration must show that the OAuth consent screen correctly displays the app name.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Your home page must be publicly accessible, and not just accessible to your
evidence.answer: The app's home page must be publicly accessible, not only accessible to logged-in users of the site.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: aren't considered valid application home pages.
evidence.answer: Links to a Google Play Store listing or a Facebook page are not considered valid application home pages.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: You must limit your use of Google user data to the practices that your published privacy policy discloses.
evidence.answer: The app's privacy policy must disclose how the app accesses, uses, stores, or shares Google user data, and the app must limit its use to those disclosed practices.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: After you publish your branding or submit a data access request, Google's Trust & Safety team may follow up by email with any additional information they need or steps you must complete.
evidence.answer: After publishing branding or submitting a data access request, Google's Trust & Safety team may email for more information or steps to complete.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Examples of sensitive scopes include reading events stored in Google Calendar, storing a new contact in Google Contacts, or deleting a YouTube video.
evidence.answer: Examples of sensitive scopes include reading events in Google Calendar, storing a new contact in Google Contacts, or deleting a YouTube video.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: You must request the narrowest scope necessary for your app's functionality and ensure data usage complies with API policies and your privacy policy.
evidence.answer: The app must request the narrowest scope necessary for its functionality.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: A user cap restricts the number of Google Accounts able to grant access to your unverified app.
evidence.answer: Unverified apps are limited by a user cap on the number of Google Accounts that can grant access.

evidence.answer: Apps in testing still show a tester warning screen, have a user cap, and have a limited refresh token lifetime.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: You must manage the list of Google Accounts that are involved in the development or testing of your app.
evidence.answer: The developer must manage the list of Google Accounts involved in development or testing.

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: scope verification process typically takes 3-5 business days to complete.
evidence.answer: The sensitive scope verification process typically takes 3-5 business days to complete.

evidence.answer: Compliant brand verification results are valid for 7 days; if not published within that time, brand verification must be run again.

evidence.question: G6

evidence.answer: The automated brand verification review usually completes in a few minutes.

evidence.answer: Google Workspace organization administrators can restrict access to sensitive scopes for their organization.

evidence.question: G8
